stem: Proton with kinetic energy of $1$ MeV moves from south to north. It gets an acceleration of $10^{12}\ \text{m/s}^2$ by an applied magnetic field (west to east). The value of magnetic field: (Rest mass of proton is $1.6 \times 10^{-27}$ kg)

A stone is thrown vertically upward. On its way up it passes point $A$ with speed of $v$, and point $B$, $3$ m higher than A, with speed $\frac{v}{2}$. The maximum height reached by stone above point B is:
solution:
$\left(\dfrac{v}{2}\right)^2 = v^2 - 2g\times3 \quad \therefore v = \sqrt{8g}$

If $h$ is the further height, then

$$0 = \left(\frac{v}{2}\right)^2 - 2gh \;\Rightarrow\; h = \frac{v^2}{8g} = \frac{8g}{8g} = 1\ \text{m}$$

stem: A block kept on a rough inclined plane, as shown in the figure, remains at rest up to a maximum force $2$ N down the inclined plane. The maximum external force up the inclined plane that does not move the block is $10$ N. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the plane is: [Take $g = 10\ \text{m/s}^2$]
solution:
From figure, $2 + mg\sin30^\circ = \mu mg\cos30^\circ$ and $10 = mg\sin30^\circ + \mu mg\cos30^\circ$

Adding and subtracting: $\mu mg\cos30^\circ = 6$ and $mg\sin30^\circ = 4$. Dividing, $\dfrac{3}{2} = \mu\sqrt3$

$\therefore$ Coefficient of friction, $\mu = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$
notes: Figure (incline 30°, 2 N down, 10 N up) appears only in the solution in the source.

stem: A Carnot engine operating between temperatures $T_1$ and $T_2$ has efficiency $0.2$. When $T_2$ is reduced by $50$ K, its efficiency increases to $0.4$. Then $T_1$ and $T_2$ are respectively
solution:
$\eta = 1 - \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} \Rightarrow 0.2 = 1 - \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} \Rightarrow \dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = 0.8 \quad \ldots(i)$

When $T_2$ is reduced by 50 K: $0.4 = 1 - \dfrac{T_2 - 50}{T_1} \Rightarrow \dfrac{T_2-50}{T_1} = 0.6 \quad \ldots(ii)$

Dividing (i) by (ii): $\dfrac{T_2}{T_2-50} = \dfrac{4}{3} \Rightarrow T_2 = 200$ K

From (ii), $T_1 = \dfrac{200-50}{0.6} = 250$ K

stem: A particle $P$ is moving in a circle of radius $a$ with a uniform speed $v$. $C$ is the centre of the circle and $AB$ is a diameter. When passing through $B$ the angular velocity of $P$ about $A$ and $C$ are in the ratio

When $M_1$ gram of ice at $-10^\circ$C (specific heat $= 0.5\ \text{cal g}^{-1}\,{}^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$) is added to $M_2$ gram of water at $50^\circ$C, finally no ice is left and the water is at $0^\circ$C. The value of latent heat of ice, in $\text{cal g}^{-1}$ is
solution:
Heat lost = Heat gained

$\Rightarrow M_2\times1\times50 = M_1\times0.5\times10 + M_1L_f$

$$\Rightarrow L_f = \frac{50M_2 - 5M_1}{M_1} = \frac{50M_2}{M_1} - 5$$

stem: Variation of current passing through a conductor as the voltage applied across its ends is varied as shown in the adjoining diagram. If the resistance $(R)$ is determined at the points $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$, we will find that
solution:
From the curve it is clear that slopes at points $A, B, C, D$ have the order $A > B > C > D$.

Resistance at any point equals the slope of the $V$ vs $i$ curve. So the order of resistance is

$R_A > R_B > R_C > R_D$.
